questions.stem: What are the two broad categories of AI and ML features that Snowflake offers?

options.text: Snowflake Cortex (LLM-based) and Snowflake ML (build your own models)
Snowflake AI Studio and Snowflake Data Science Workbench
Snowflake AutoML and Snowflake Deep Learning
Snowflake NLP and Snowflake Computer Vision

explanation.correct: Snowflake offers Snowflake Cortex (a suite of LLM-based AI features for unstructured data and intelligent assistance) and Snowflake ML (for building your own custom models).

distractors.B: AI Studio and Data Science Workbench are not the named categories of Snowflake AI/ML features.
distractors.C: AutoML and Deep Learning are not the official category names used by Snowflake.
distractors.D: NLP and Computer Vision are use cases, not the two broad Snowflake AI/ML categories.

questions.stem: Which privilege is required at the account level to call Cortex AI Functions?

explanation.correct: To call Cortex AI Functions, your role needs the USE AI FUNCTIONS account-level privilege and one of the CORTEX_USER or AI_FUNCTIONS_USER database roles.

distractors.A: EXECUTE AI FUNCTIONS is not a valid Snowflake privilege name.
distractors.B: CREATE AI FUNCTION is not the required privilege; you don't create AI functions, you call them.
distractors.D: MANAGE AI FEATURES is not a valid Snowflake privilege.

questions.stem: What is the minimum advance notice Snowflake provides before deprecating a General Availability (GA) model used by Cortex AI features?

explanation.correct: For GA models, Snowflake makes reasonable efforts to provide at least 60 days advance notice prior to deprecation.

distractors.A: 30 days is below the minimum notice period for GA models.
distractors.B: 90 days exceeds the stated minimum of 60 days.
distractors.D: 14 days is far below the GA model deprecation notice period; shorter notice may apply to preview models only.

questions.stem: Which TWO Cortex AI Functions aggregate data across multiple rows and are NOT subject to context window limitations? (Select TWO)

explanation.correct: AI_AGG aggregates a text column and returns insights across multiple rows, and AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG aggregates and returns a summary across multiple rows. Both are not subject to context window limitations.

distractors.A: AI_COMPLETE generates completions for individual prompts and IS subject to context window limits.
distractors.D: AI_SENTIMENT extracts sentiment from individual text inputs, not across rows.
distractors.E: AI_EMBED generates embeddings for individual inputs, not multi-row aggregations.

questions.stem: Which THREE security principles apply to Snowflake AI Features? (Select THREE)

options.text: All AI models run inside Snowflake's security and governance perimeter
Snowflake uses Customer Data to improve models for the broader customer base
Your data is not available to other customers or model developers
You control your team's use of AI features through role-based access control
All AI features require Enterprise Edition or higher
AI model outputs are automatically encrypted with customer-managed keys

explanation.correct: Snowflake AI Features run inside the security perimeter, data is not shared with other customers/model developers, and access is controlled through familiar RBAC.

distractors.B: Snowflake explicitly states it never uses Customer Data to train models available to the customer base.
distractors.E: Not all AI features require Enterprise Edition; many are available in Standard Edition.
distractors.F: There is no requirement for customer-managed key encryption specifically for AI outputs.

questions.scenario: A data analyst wants to classify customer support tickets into categories like 'billing', 'technical', and 'general' using natural language.
questions.stem: Which Cortex AI Function should they use?

explanation.correct: AI_CLASSIFY classifies text or images into user-defined categories, making it ideal for categorizing support tickets.

distractors.A: AI_SENTIMENT extracts sentiment (positive/negative/neutral), not custom categories.
distractors.B: AI_FILTER returns True/False for a given input, not category labels.
distractors.C: AI_EXTRACT extracts specific information from input, not classify into categories.

questions.scenario: A developer wants to count the number of tokens in a prompt before sending it to AI_COMPLETE to ensure it doesn't exceed the model's context window.
questions.stem: Which function should they use?

explanation.correct: AI_COUNT_TOKENS is a helper function that returns the token count for an input text based on the specified model or Cortex function.

distractors.A: LEN() returns the character length of a string, not the token count for a model.
distractors.C: TOKEN_LENGTH() is not a valid Snowflake function.
distractors.D: CHAR_LENGTH() returns character count, which is different from token count used by LLMs.

questions.scenario: A company needs to extract text from scanned PDF documents stored in a Snowflake stage for downstream analytics.
questions.stem: Which Cortex AI Function supports this use case?

explanation.correct: AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT extracts text (using OCR mode) or text with layout information (using LAYOUT mode) from documents stored in internal or external stages.

distractors.A: AI_EXTRACT extracts structured information from text/images but is not specifically for parsing document files from stages with OCR.
distractors.C: AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG summarizes across rows; it doesn't extract text from documents.
distractors.D: AI_COMPLETE generates completions; it doesn't perform document parsing or OCR.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Cortex AI Function deployment are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: All LLMs are deployed within the Snowflake Service perimeter
LLMs are hosted by third-party providers outside of Snowflake's infrastructure
Cortex AI Functions are optimized for throughput and best suited for batch processing
For interactive low-latency use cases, Cortex AI Functions are preferred over the REST API
Customer data is sent to model developers for inference

explanation.correct: All LLMs that Snowflake provides access to via AI Features are deployed within the Snowflake Service perimeter. Cortex AI Functions are optimized for throughput and batch processing of large tables.

distractors.B: LLMs run inside Snowflake's perimeter, not at third-party infrastructure.
distractors.D: For interactive/low-latency use cases, the REST API is recommended over AI Functions.
distractors.E: Data is not shared with model developers; it stays within Snowflake's governance boundary.

questions.scenario: A data engineer wants to use AI_FILTER in a WHERE clause to filter rows based on whether the text content matches a natural language condition.
questions.stem: What does AI_FILTER return for each row?

explanation.correct: AI_FILTER returns True or False for a given text or image input, allowing you to filter results in SELECT, WHERE, or JOIN ON clauses.

distractors.A: AI_SIMILARITY returns a similarity score, not AI_FILTER.
distractors.C: Category labels are returned by AI_CLASSIFY, not AI_FILTER.
distractors.D: Embedding vectors are returned by AI_EMBED, not AI_FILTER.

questions.scenario: An administrator wants to remove PII from text data before storing it in a reporting table.
questions.stem: Which Cortex AI Function should they use?

explanation.correct: AI_REDACT redacts personally identifiable information (PII) from text.

distractors.A: AI_EXTRACT extracts information from input, not redact PII.
distractors.B: AI_FILTER returns True/False for filtering, not for redaction.
distractors.D: AI_CLASSIFY categorizes text, not redact sensitive information.

questions.scenario: A team is reviewing the Cortex AI Function categories to understand which functions are helper functions versus task-specific AI functions.
questions.stem: Which TWO functions are classified as helper functions? (Select TWO)

explanation.correct: TO_FILE (creates references to files in stages) and AI_COUNT_TOKENS (counts tokens in input) are helper functions designed to support other Cortex AI Functions.

distractors.A: AI_COMPLETE is a core Cortex AI function for generating completions, not a helper.
distractors.D: AI_TRANSLATE is a task-specific AI function for translation.
distractors.E: AI_SENTIMENT is a task-specific AI function for sentiment extraction.

questions.scenario: A media company needs to transcribe audio files from customer calls stored in a Snowflake stage.
questions.stem: Which Cortex AI Function extracts text, timestamps, and speaker information from audio and video files?

explanation.correct: AI_TRANSCRIBE transcribes audio and video files stored in a stage, extracting text, timestamps, and speaker information.

distractors.A: AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT processes documents (PDFs, images), not audio/video files.
distractors.B: AI_EXTRACT extracts structured data from text/images, not audio transcription.
distractors.C: AI_COMPLETE generates text completions but does not transcribe audio.

questions.scenario: A developer wants to calculate how similar two pieces of text are for a recommendation engine.
questions.stem: Which Cortex AI Function calculates embedding similarity between two inputs?

explanation.correct: AI_SIMILARITY calculates the embedding similarity between two inputs, useful for recommendation engines and content matching.

distractors.A: AI_EMBED generates an embedding vector for a single input; it does not compute similarity between two inputs.
distractors.B: AI_CLASSIFY categorizes inputs into predefined classes, not measure similarity.
distractors.D: AI_FILTER returns True/False based on a condition, not a similarity score.

questions.scenario: An organization is evaluating the model lifecycle stages for Cortex AI features to understand when models are production-ready.
questions.stem: Which THREE stages are part of the model lifecycle for models in Cortex? (Select THREE)

explanation.correct: Models follow a lifecycle of Private Preview → Public Preview → General Availability (GA) → Legacy → End of Life (EOL). Private Preview, GA, and Legacy are three of these stages.

distractors.C: Beta Testing is not a named stage in Snowflake's model lifecycle.
distractors.E: Experimental is not a named stage; the earliest stage is Private Preview.
distractors.F: Candidate Release is not part of Snowflake's model lifecycle terminology.

questions.scenario: A team wants to use AI_COMPLETE to generate summaries of individual customer feedback entries.
questions.stem: Which database role must their role have to call this function?

explanation.correct: To call Cortex AI Functions, your role needs the USE AI FUNCTIONS privilege and one of the CORTEX_USER or AI_FUNCTIONS_USER database roles.

distractors.A: AI_ADMIN is not a valid Snowflake database role.
distractors.C: ML_ENGINEER is not a valid Snowflake database role for this purpose.
distractors.D: DATA_SCIENTIST is not a valid Snowflake database role.

questions.scenario: A product manager wants to understand which Snowflake Cortex features are available beyond just LLM functions.
questions.stem: Which THREE features are part of the Snowflake Cortex suite? (Select THREE)

explanation.correct: Cortex Fine-tuning, Cortex Analyst, and Cortex Search are all part of the Snowflake Cortex suite of AI features.

distractors.B: Feature Store is part of Snowflake ML, not Snowflake Cortex.
distractors.D: ML Functions are part of Snowflake ML, not the Cortex suite.
distractors.F: Model Registry is part of Snowflake ML, not Snowflake Cortex.

questions.scenario: A model update changes the structure of the output returned by a Cortex AI function.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about how model behavior changes are communicated to customers are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: All model updates require customer action
Model deprecations are bundled into regular release cycles
Changes to required syntax are considered behavior changes
Output structure changes are communicated through Behavior Change Releases (BCRs)
Improvements that don't change interaction are communicated via What's New only

explanation.correct: Changes to output structure and changes to required syntax are both considered behavior changes communicated through BCRs.

distractors.A: Not all updates require action; only behavior changes that impact existing workflows do.
distractors.B: Model deprecations are communicated separately from bundled releases.
distractors.E: While improvements go to What's New, this alone doesn't describe behavior change communication.

questions.scenario: A data engineer needs to generate embedding vectors for text data to use in a similarity search application.
questions.stem: Which Cortex AI Function generates embedding vectors for text or image inputs?

explanation.correct: AI_EMBED generates an embedding vector for a text or image input, which can be used for similarity search, clustering, and classification tasks.

distractors.A: AI_SIMILARITY compares two inputs for similarity but doesn't generate the embeddings themselves.
distractors.B: AI_COMPLETE generates text completions, not embedding vectors.
distractors.D: AI_CLASSIFY categorizes inputs into classes, not generate embedding vectors.

questions.scenario: A compliance officer wants to understand how preview Cortex AI Functions differ from GA functions regarding data classification.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Cortex AI Function data classification designations are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Preview functions are designated as Covered AI Features
GA functions are designated as Covered AI Features
Input data is classified as Usage Data
Output data is classified as Usage Data
All Cortex functions are designated as Experimental AI Features

explanation.correct: GA functions are Covered AI Features, and the input data classification is Usage Data while output is Customer Data.

distractors.A: Preview functions are designated as Preview AI Features, not Covered.
distractors.D: Output data is classified as Customer Data, not Usage Data.
distractors.E: Experimental AI Features is not a valid designation in Snowflake.
